summary.headline: L&T Finance posted record Q2 FY27 PAT of ₹975 Cr (up 33% YoY) with credit cost easing to 2.46% and RoA at 2.60%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 delivered record consolidated PAT of ₹975 Cr, up 33% YoY, with consolidated book at ₹1,36,635 Cr (up 28% YoY) and RoA of 2.60%. Credit cost moderated 8 bps QoQ to 2.46%, and NIMs plus fees held at 10.48%, aided by a 25 bps fall in weighted average cost of borrowing. Rural disbursements were deliberately tempered on monsoon-related risk, while Personal Loans stalled sequentially on partner-level Cyclops migrations. Management also flagged the draft IRDAI commission consultation as a potential revenue headwind, which it said it has not yet quantified.

segments.name: Rural Business Finance
segments.commentary: Disbursements ₹6,356 Cr (up 1% YoY); book ₹33,465 Cr (up 22% YoY). Collection efficiency 99.7%-99.8%. Drought-declared-area book about ₹1,033 Cr, or 3.3% of the ₹31,500 Cr rural group loan and business loan book.

segments.name: Farmer Finance
segments.commentary: Disbursements ₹1,643 Cr (down 1% YoY); book ₹17,397 Cr (up 9% YoY).

segments.name: Two-Wheelers
segments.commentary: Disbursements ₹3,170 Cr (up 26% YoY); book ₹16,158 Cr (up 24% YoY). 92% of disbursements in prime segment; Cyclops 90+ DPD about 1.2%. September 0 DPD collection dip attributed to a self-cure experiment, with October back near 99%.

segments.name: Personal Loans
segments.commentary: Record disbursements ₹4,233 Cr (up 45% YoY); book ₹18,664 Cr (up 72% YoY). Sequentially flattish due to partner-by-partner Cyclops migration; monthly run rate now ₹1,400-1,500 Cr, targeting ₹1,700-1,800 Cr.

segments.name: Mortgage (HL/LAP)
segments.commentary: Disbursements ₹2,926 Cr (up 8% YoY); book ₹32,846 Cr (up 20% YoY). Launched Aarambh economical housing loans (₹20-50 lakh tickets). Management says LAP delinquency is about 10% of industry delinquency on its index.

segments.name: SME Finance
segments.commentary: Disbursements ₹1,820 Cr (up 24% YoY); book ₹495 Cr (up 27% YoY). About 80% of portfolio covered under CGTMSE.

segments.name: Gold Finance
segments.commentary: Disbursements ₹3,237 Cr (up 229% YoY); closing book ₹5,043 Cr (up 242% YoY). 502 active branches after 172 added in H1 FY27; about 110 branches above ₹15 Cr AUM.

guidance_outlook: Credit cost to reach 2%-2.2% corridor by Q4 FY27.
RoA to exit Q4 FY27 at 2.8%-3.0%; Lakshya 2031 RoA target 3.0%-3.2% for FY31.
NIMs + fees to stay around the middle of the 10%-10.5% corridor for next couple of quarters.
Cost of funds: management expects 2-3 more repo hikes at most (December, February); base cost of borrowing now 6.95%; incremental borrowing yields up 30-50 bps.
Gold loan branches to reach about 800 by end-2026 and about 2,000 in the long run; Gold AUM target ₹40,000-45,000 Cr (14%-15% of AUM) by FY31.
Book CAGR of 20%+ over Lakshya period; Q3 FY27 expected to show strong momentum with rural disbursements rising from festive season.
Investor Digital Day on 15 December 2026; full Hercules agentic cross-sell engine by early December 2026.
capex_capacity: Sampoorna multi-product branches at 151, of which 33 integrated with Gold Loan business.
Plans for 500 Gold branches and 200 Micro LAP branches; branches reach breakeven in about 6 months.
Opex to stay elevated for at least a couple more years due to branch rollouts, but offset by Cyclops and bot-led collection efficiencies.

Payments platform: UPI stack live in closed user group testing; agentic commerce stack with Pine Labs to be unveiled at RAISE 2026; Prepaid Issuer licence applied for, PPI products targeted for FY28 subject to RBI approval.
demand_pricing: Rural demand muted; management attributes flat rural disbursements to both risk guardrails and weak customer demand after below-normal monsoon (87% of LPA). Kharif sowing down 1.0% YoY at 101% of normal acreage.
Personal Loan sequential disbursement flat due to Cyclops implementation; large partnerships now 40% of PL originations and expected to rise.
Yields: management says risk-based pricing has recovered 70-75 bps of the 75-100 bps yield loss from Cyclops migration in Two-Wheelers, and expects yields to hold up.
Management said the mix shift away from Microfinance (grew ~5% when market de-grew) and towards Micro LAP, PL, Gold, and SME should keep yields up.
Cost of funds: CPs rose from about 5% to 8% of mix; PSL share fell from 26% to about 23%; PTCs about 5% at cheap rates; base cost now 6.95%, first time below 7%.
Fee and other income dipped QoQ because about ₹4,000 Cr of excess Q1 liquidity earned lower income; normal range is 180-185 bps, and liquidity was 20-22 bps lower this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How will the repo rate hike be passed through, and what repricing exposure exists?
qa_highlights.answer: Only the ~₹25,000 Cr variable-rate home loan book reprices. Asset and liability fixed/floating mix is matched; management expects NIMs + fees to stay mid-corridor of 10%-10.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did portfolio cost of borrowing fall 25 bps when only incremental borrowings are at lower rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management replaced high-cost WCDLs and term loans that were drawn during Q1 excess liquidity (about ₹4,000 Cr); average liquidity fell to ₹9,500-10,000 Cr. CP tenors were extended to 6-12 months and PTC and sub-debt were raised.

qa_highlights.question: Is the IRDAI commission consultation a risk to the 3% RoA target, and what offsets exist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact is not quantified and the draft is under discussion; SRO FIDC is engaging the regulator for a glide path. Offsets cited include cross-sell via Hercules, PPI and payments fee income, and a one-to-one retail insurance channel accelerating in H2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the exposure to drought-affected states and rural underwriting changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Drought-declared-area book is about ₹1,033 Cr (3.3% of ₹31,500 Cr rural group and business loan book). Guardrails tightened in those districts; no visible risk build-up per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Two-Wheeler collection efficiency dip in September?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was an AI-based self-cure experiment (self-cure about 43%, targeting 50%-55%) that overshot; October recovered to about 99%, and it is not structural.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Personal Loan run rate and outlook after the sequential flattening?
qa_highlights.answer: Monthly run rate is ₹1,400-1,500 Cr, with interim target of ₹1,700-1,800 Cr; onboarding a new partner now takes 3-4 months versus 2 months earlier, and one large partner remains to migrate.

qa_highlights.question: Is there gold loan stress such as GS2 formation or bullet-loan delinquency?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said collections are business as usual; about 15 months in, no loss episode; auctions recovered over 140% of dues. Early delinquency seen only in recent bullet-loan cohorts, per RBI LTV norms effective 1 April.

risks_watch: Monsoon and drought exposure in Karnataka, Maharashtra, AP, Telangana; rabi outcome and rural cash flows.
Further repo hikes (2-3 expected) and incremental borrowing costs 30-50 bps higher; sustainability of 6.95% base cost.
Final IRDAI insurance commission framework and resulting RoA/fee impact; management has not quantified it.
Credit cost must fall from 2.46% to 2%-2.2% by Q4 FY27; Personal Loan and Two-Wheeler collection efficiency after the September dip.
Gold loan book growth on new branches and early bullet-loan delinquencies on post-1 April cohorts.
Rural disbursement pickup in Q3 after guardrail tightening.
key_quotes: We would like to reiterate that we are confident of achieving our guided credit cost corridor of 2%-2.2% by Q4FY27.
As the framework is still a draft consultation paper, it would be premature to quantify the final impact.
I'm being very, very candid on the call. We don't want to overreact to that because it is currently under discussion.
It is born out of an experiment and it is nothing structural.
So, for us, LAP remains our least concern.
summary.management_tone: Confident on franchise, asset quality and the Lakshya 2031 trajectory, repeatedly reiterating credit cost, RoA and cost-of-funds targets. Cautious and evasive on the IRDAI commission impact (declined to quantify, "don't want to overreact") and on the full-year cost-of-funds path, and candid about the Cyclops-driven Personal Loan slowdown and the September Two-Wheeler collection experiment.
